To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

influenza virus ribonucleoproteins gain access to the export pathway via chromatin targeting and that this targeting brings vRNPs into association with the Ran guanine nucleotide exchange factor, Rcc1.

influenza virus ribonucleoproteins gain preferential access through the nuclear pore to the cellular export machinery by targeting the Ran guanine nucleotide exchange factor Rcc1 at the sites of chromatin in the nucleus.
vRNPs gain access to Crm1-mediated nuclear export by tethering to chromatin, which brings them in close association with Rcc-1, the RanGTP generator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of influenza virus replication and the interactions between virus and host cell.
how influenza viruses replicate in the nucleus of the host cell and how newly synthesized viral ribonucleocapsids are exported from the nucleus to the cytoplams.
the mechanisms of influenza virus replication, and in particular the export of the viral genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
influenza viruses gain preferentially access to the cellular export machinery by targeting viral ribonucleotide protein complexes to the host cell chromatin.
influenza viruses hijack the host cell machinery by targeting their export complexes at the chromatin.
the influenza virus RNP complex gains preferential access to the host-cell export machinery by targeting the vRNP to the chromatin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
influenza vRNPs gain preferential access of the cellular export machinery by targeting to the chromatin.
influenza viruses gain preferentially access to host-cell export machinery through chromatin targeting of the viral ribonucleotide complex.
influenza viruses target their own vRNPs to the sites of RanGTP generation, which allows them to gain preferential access over other nuclear Crm 1 substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
influenza vRNPs gain access to the host-cell nuclear export machinery through targeting of viral ribonulceoprotein complexes (RNPs) to the chromatin.
